描述_EN: the emperors of the ming and qing dynasties (1368-1911) were patrons of buddhism, and woven silks were frequently used as relic or sutra covers (volumes of buddhist litanies), or for decoration. this fragment was probably woven for use on a buddhist object, although similarly designed textiles were used in japan in tea ceremonies. such textiles woven in patchwork colours were supposed to be reminiscent of early monastic robes.
描述_ZN: 明清两代的皇帝都是佛教的拥护者，编织的丝绸经常被用作文物或经书的封面（佛教的经卷），或用于装饰。 这个片段可能是为佛教物品而编织的，尽管类似的设计纺织品在日本被用于茶道。 这种用拼接颜色编织的纺织品应该是让人联想到早期的僧侣袍。
